newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire terrier is top dog at Crufts show.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire terrier is top dog at Crufts show.

text.p: Justin, a five-year-old Yorkshire terrier, defeated thousands of other contestants on Sunday to win the "best of show" at Crufts, Britain's premier dog show.
"He was very well presented and he's an all-round top dog," a spokesman for Crufts said after the contest. "It's not common for a terrier to win best of show."

Justin, or Champion of Ozmillion Mystification as he is registered with the Kennel Club, is owned by a London antiques dealer. He won the toy dog category before taking the top award and receiving the Kedell Memorial Trophy named after the show's manager from 1894 to 1924.
Dexter, an American cocker spaniel, came second.
"This is the second time Justin won his group and the second time he was in the final lineup for best of show," the spokesman added.

Organised by the Kennel Club, the four-day event which featured more than 15,000 exhibitors and attracted 100,000 visitors to Britain's National Exhibition centre in Birmingham is considered the top event for dog owners.

The dogs are divided into six groups -- hounds, gun dogs, terriers, utility dogs, working and toys -- and the best of show dog is chosen from the winner of each category, based on physique, temperament and handling.
